Title: October 1, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Meeting (Regular Meeting)

Topic1.Title: Amend Agenda to Add Front Range Passenger Rail Sales Tax Discussion
Topic1.Summary: Council voted to amend the agenda to add item 8A, the Front Range passenger rail sales tax measure discussion. The amendment passed. Council later took a straw poll and unanimously directed staff to prepare a resolution of support for the measure at a future business meeting.

Topic2.Title: Public Participation and Open Comment
Topic2.Summary: Nineteen speakers addressed topics including the CU South development and flood mitigation, the Boulderthon road closures, small cell tower installation, the Belmont homeless site, Gunbarrel parks and safety, Spruce Pool, and various national and international issues. Staff responded to several concerns, including tenant union resources, small cell tower limitations, the Boulderthon, CU South closure notification, and the Belmont site plan. Council members acknowledged staff and offered brief comments.

Topic3.Title: Consent Agenda
Topic3.Summary: Council approved consent agenda items 3A through 3H unanimously after a motion and second. No questions or comments were raised on the consent items.

Topic4.Title: Call-Up Check-In: Nuropa Campus Site Review (LUR2026-0000003)
Topic4.Summary: Council reviewed a site review application to redevelop the Nuropa campus with about 135 residential units and a height modification to 55 feet. Council Member Winer raised concerns about shadow and setback impacts on Marine Street, and the applicant stated the buildings sit at least 40 feet from the west property line and comply with solar standards. No council member called up the item.

Topic5.Title: Public Hearing: 2027 Budget and Associated Ordinances
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented the 2027 recommended budget totaling $552.6 million, with a $417.2 million operating budget and $135.4 million capital budget, addressing a $6.3 million general fund gap. Council asked questions about Sundance revenues, wildfire funding, the Ranger Cottage and CIP reallocation options, the Care program, and the Parks and Recreation board's dissent. After public comment and extended debate, council did not adopt any budget amendments and passed ordinances 8777 through 8780 as proposed.
